service.description: How the current user's calendar opens and new events start, from the user's preferences with the defaults: view (CALENDAR_DEFAULT_VIEW: day, workweek, week, month or agenda; week), weekStart (CALENDAR_WEEK_START, 0 Sunday, 1 Monday or 6 Saturday; 0), workStart and workEnd (CALENDAR_WORK_START and CALENDAR_WORK_END, HH:mm; 09:00 and 17:00), workDays (CALENDAR_WORK_DAYS, weekday numbers 0-6; 1,2,3,4,5), defaultDuration (CALENDAR_DEFAULT_DURATION, minutes; 60), defaultReminder (CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REMINDER, minutes before, empty for none; 10), showDeclined (CALENDAR_SHOW_DECLINED, Y or N; N), showWeekNumbers (CALENDAR_SHOW_WEEK_NUMBERS; N), showTasks (CALENDAR_SHOW_TASKS; N) and the calendars the user turned off (CALENDAR_HIDDEN, a comma list).

Saves the CalendarDefaults of Settings/Preferences as the current user's preferences (get#CalendarDefaults) and, with defaultCalendarId, makes that one of the user's own personal calendars the default (mantle.work.CalendarServices.update#Calendar). A field left out (null) is not changed.

Working hours as Mantle reads them for free/busy (mantle.work.EventServices.get#FreeBusy, Find a time) and business time (mantle.work.CalendarServices.get#BusinessTimeDue): with no party, the current user's from the CalendarDefaults preferences (the working days and hours), a WetAvailable work effort of the user's party repeating weekly in the user's time zone, made once (sourceReferenceId BossWorkingHours) and changed after; with partyId (a service team, from Customer Service's AgentTeams) the days and hours given on the party's schedule calendar, from fromDate. Mantle's mantle.work.CalendarServices.store#WorkingHours stores them and checks who may.

What the calendar rail shows, kept as the current user's preferences: the calendars turned off (hiddenCalendarIds, CALENDAR_HIDDEN), the tasks (showTasks, CALENDAR_SHOW_TASKS) and declined invitations (showDeclined, CALENDAR_SHOW_DECLINED). A field left out is not changed.

What the calendar needs before its events: the user's calendars for the rail (mine, subscriptions and shared with me, from mantle.work.CalendarServices.get#UserCalendars, the default made on first use), each with whether it is shown and may take new events, a subscription's last fetch with a warning when it failed; the calendar defaults; the user's time zone, today and now in it; the user's party and name; the bookable meeting rooms for the quick event. A part that fails is logged and named in failedSources.

The events of the grid from start to end (days, yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone): get#FullCalendarData over the calendars of calendarIds (the ones the user has on) plus every event the user is on, recurring events expanded, cancelled ones left out and the user's declined invitations unless showDeclined, whatever calendar they are in (get#FullCalendarData leaves them out, and gives each event's location and organizer). An event of the user's own calendars that is only in calendars the user turned off is left out too (an invitation from someone else always shows). Each is {key, workEffortId, title, start and end (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, or yyyy-MM-dd days for an all-day event with end the day after its last), allDay, color (its calendar's), calendarId, statusId, partyStatusId (the user's answer: WeptOffered is an invitation to answer), recurring, recurringEventId, instanceStart, freeBusyOnly, location, canEdit (organizer or an editor of a calendar that holds it for its editors, not one it was only put in to be seen, and never an event an application keeps: check#EventAccess's rule, Commons calendar editors of Nov 12, 2026), hasAttendees, isOrganizer, url}. With showTasks the user's tasks come too, by their due date ({kind: task, ...}). A part that fails is logged and named in failedSources.

The event popover: an event the user may see (check#EventAccess, or the record visibility rule of get#RecordLinkInfo; visible false otherwise) with when (instanceStart for an instance of a recurring event), where (location, meeting rooms and equipment with their booking status), the join link (infoUrl, else the first web address in the location or description), the organizer, the attendees with their answers, the user's own answer, its calendar and what the user may do.

actions.script: event = Object.assign({}, facts.event || {}, {canEdit: !!access.canEdit, isOrganizer: !!access.isOrganizer, isAttendee: !!access.isAttendee, canRsvp: !!access.isAttendee && !access.isOrganizer && facts.event?.statusId !== 'WeCancelled'})

service.description: Whether the current user may see an event (WetEvent): check#EventAccess (organizer, attendee, a calendar it is in, visible to all users), else the record visibility rule of get#RecordLinkInfo with checkOnly (IronStone R5, R28: its parties and organizations; ADMIN sees all); and what the user may do with it (canEdit as organizer or editor of a calendar that holds it for its editors, never an event an application keeps: managedBy says where that one is changed; Commons calendar editors, Nov 12, 2026). need view adds "not available" when the user may not see it, edit also when the user may not change it; check answers without an error. A production run is not found (impl-manufacturing F39).

parameter.name: managedBy
parameter.description: Where the event is changed, when an application keeps it (check#EventAccess)

service.description: The facts of an event shared by the popover and EventDetail, for a caller that checked access: name, status, when (whenText; startText and endText as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, or days for an all-day event), the recurrence and its summary, the series and instance, location, join link, description, visibility, the calendars it is in, organizer, attendees (with answer, required or optional, invited or not), meeting rooms and equipment with their booking status, and the user's own answer. An instance left out of its series (an EXDATE) is cancelled and excluded.

A recurrence rule in words: "Weekly on Monday and Wednesday, 10 times", "Every 2 weeks on Friday until Dec 31, 2026", "Monthly on day 15", "Monthly on the second Tuesday", "Yearly on Mar 4", "Every weekday"; the rule itself when it is one this does not read.

parameter.name: startText
parameter.description: The first instance (yyyy-MM-dd or yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm), for the day of a rule without BYDAY

service.description: An RRULE from the recurrence editor's fields: freq (NONE, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or YEARLY; a preset also: WEEKDAYS), interval, byDay (weekday codes MO..SU for WEEKLY), monthlyBy (day: the start's day of the month, weekday: the start's nth weekday, last for the last one), ends (never, until or count) with untilDate (yyyy-MM-dd, the last day, in the user's time zone) or count, and the start (yyyy-MM-dd or yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm) for the defaults. Empty for NONE.

The recurrence editor's fields of an RRULE (make#RRule's inputs): freq, interval, byDay, monthlyBy, ends, untilDate (yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone) and count; custom true when the rule has parts the editor does not show (it is then kept as it is unless changed).

The calendar's quick event (a click or a drag on the grid): ironstone.commons.QuickCreateServices.create#Event (in calendarId, the user's default calendar by default; attendees invited) from start to end (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the user's time zone; days for an all-day event, end the last day), then a repeat preset (none, daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly, yearly: store#EventRecurrence), the user's reminder (reminderMinutes before; store#WorkEffortReminders) and a meeting room (book#Resource: by its policy booked or requested). A room or reminder that fails is a warning and the event stays.
The user's answer to an event (accept, tentative or decline) with an optional message (mantle.work.EventServices.respond#EventInvitation), the organizer told; a user who is not on it is refused.

set.from: ec.l10n.localize({accept: 'You accepted', tentative: 'You answered maybe', decline: 'You declined'}[String(response).toLowerCase()] || 'Answer saved')

service.description: The calendar's search: events (not cancelled) whose name or location has the text and that the user owns, is on, or that are in one of the user's calendars, upcoming first then the most recent past ones, at most 40, each with its start day to go to.

People to invite: people (with a user or not; a personal contact only for its owner, as mantle.party.PartyServices.search#Person finds them) whose name or user name has the term, as drop-down options (value the party).

The current user's calendars as Settings/Calendars shows them (mantle.work.CalendarServices.get#UserCalendars): mine (owned, the default first), subscriptions with their feed's last fetch and status, and shared with me; for each the user manages, its current shares (to a user, group or party, with the permission) and whether it has a publish link. Shares are read through check#CalendarAccess (manage) only (IronStone R21).

Fetches a subscription calendar the user manages now (mantle.work.CalendarServices.fetch#CalendarSubscriptions for it, forced), and answers its fetch status: ok, or error with the reason, which the subscription keeps.

A calendar the user may view as an .ics file (mantle.work.CalendarServices.export#Calendar), written to the user's own export folder, dbresource://ironstone/CalendarExport/{userId}/, for the screen to send as a download.

actions.script: location = null if (!ec.user.userId) { ec.message.addError(ec.l10n.localize('An export needs a user')); return } const out = ec.service.sync().name('mantle.work.CalendarServices.export#Calendar').parameters({calendarId: calendarId}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return fileName = String(out.fileName || 'calendar.ics').replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9 _.-]/g, '_').replace(/\s+/g, '-') location = `dbresource://ironstone/CalendarExport/${ec.user.userId}/${fileName}` ec.resource.getLocationReference(location).putText(out.fileText || '')

service.description: The token check of the public calendar page's token-route (/cal/<token>; the framework calls it with token and routeName before anything of the page runs). An unknown or malformed token, or a share that also names a user, group or party, is not valid, so the route answers its "link expired or not found" page. A publish link is valid: routeContext {expired: false, calendarName, color, needsPassword} while it is current, and {expired: true} once it has ended (or not started), so the page can say so. Read only; the page's calls check the token again. The password is not checked here: a current link with a password still reaches the page.

The events of a published calendar for its public page. The token is checked first. A current link with a password and none given answers needsPassword and no events, without an error, so the page can ask. A wrong password is "The password is not right" and no events. Otherwise mantle.work.CalendarServices.get#PublishedCalendarEvents gives that calendar's events for start and end (yyyy-MM-dd), as Busy when the link is free/busy only.
